articles.title: PM Modi interacts with startup CEOs from Space Sector | Akashvani News - Newsonair
articles.content: News On AIR | August 23, 2026 1:59 PM PM Modi interacts with startup CEOs from Space Sector Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that space sector startups have shown their trust in the government. During an interaction with the startup CEOs of the space sector, Mr Modi urged the CEOs to remain consistent in their efforts and build a robust space-sector ecosystem capable of attracting talent from across the world. He noted that an enabling environment must be created in the country where people from across the world see India as the preferred destination to build their careers and future in the space sector. Mr Modi said that India is highly competitive in terms of cost, and have quality talent with a strong risk-taking capacity. The Prime Minister said that this combination gives the country the potential to establish itself rapidly as a leading player in the global space sector. During the interaction, Chief Executive Officer of India’s first space-tech unicorn, Skyroot Aerospace, Pawan Kumar Chandana thanked Mr Modi for opening up the space sector. He said that his company has built three factories and already has the capacity to produce one rocket per month. Mr Chandana added that on 18th of July this year, they successfully launched India’s first privately developed rocket.

articles.title: Create ecosystem that attracts global space talent to India: PM Modi | DD News
articles.content: 4 hours ago | PM Modi Create ecosystem that attracts global space talent to India: PM Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday interacted with CEOs of Indian space startups and highlighted the importance of predictable policymaking, global opportunities and India’s competitive strengths as the country’s private space sector expands. During the interaction, PM Modi praised entrepreneurs for taking risks and venturing into the emerging space sector, while emphasising the need for policy consistency to build confidence among investors and startups. “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” the Prime Minister said. The CEO of Skyroot described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and referred to its successful July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. The CEO said the launch was only a “warm-up” and that the company aims to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year. The CEO also said Skyroot has established three factories and has the capacity to produce one rocket per month, with plans to eventually scale up to one launch per week and, subsequently, several launches a day. PM Modi also discussed investor confidence following the launch. One startup CEO said the company had received eight launch contracts in the past month after a single launch, most of them from international customers. Highlighting the global visibility such breakthroughs can create for Indian startups, PM Modi said the world should increasingly look towards Indian companies once they demonstrate capabilities in the space sector. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” he said. The Prime Minister also stressed the potential for India to emerge as a global hub for space talent and innovation. During the interaction, a CEO said Indian citizens based in the US and Europe were seeking to return and work with Indian space companies following the opening up of the sector. PM Modi said India should create an ecosystem that attracts talent from across the world and encourages people to build their careers in the country. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” he said. The CEOs also shared their plans and technologies across a range of emerging areas, including a global ground station network, robotic spacecraft designed to capture and remove defunct satellites from orbit, docking and refuelling technologies, and satellites capable of manufacturing pharmaceuticals in space. An entrepreneur described his company as India’s first space-pharma startup. Another startup representative said the company was planning to take its innovation to 10 lakh farmers. articles.title: PM Modi Meets India Space Startup Founders | Vision for Space Economy - Bhaskar English
articles.content: English News Tech science PM Modi Meets India Space Startup Founders | Vision For Space Economy India will build petrol pumps & manufacture medicines in space: Startup founders disclose plans on meeting with PM Modi 7 hours ago Copy link Petrol pumps in space, garbage-removing robots, and medicines floating in the air. India's space sector is now working on making technology seen in films a reality. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a special conversation with founders of 20 space startups in the country. The PM assured that the government will never let go of entrepreneurs' hands. Those who take risks will get full support. This conversation took place on August 21, but the video was released today on August 23. Read the highlights of this conversation... Skyroot's goal to launch a rocket every month Skyroot informed PM Modi that on July 18, satellites were successfully placed in orbit from India's first private rocket. The company has now set up 3 factories, which have the capacity to build one rocket every month. The company's plan is to launch one rocket every month. The next target is one every week and in the future, several rockets every day. Hyderabad's Skyroot Aerospace launched India's first private orbital rocket Vikram-1 on Saturday, July 18. After this successful launch, PM Modi spoke with the startup founder over the phone. Petrol pumps, cleaning robots and medicine-making satellites Indian startups are working on several new technologies: Space Petrol Pump: A company is developing docking and refueling technology that will refuel satellites in space itself. Debris Removal: Work is underway on a robotic spacecraft that will capture useless and 'dead' satellites floating in space and remove them from orbit. Space Pharma: A startup is preparing satellites that will manufacture medicines in space's zero-gravity and bring them to Earth. Learn about Space Petrol Pump and Space Pharma Just like we go to a pump when our vehicle runs out of petrol on the road, similarly satellites run out of fuel in space. An Indian company is developing technology that will connect with satellites flying in the air and refuel them like petrol-diesel. This will prevent satellites worth crores from becoming useless. Meanwhile, when a medicine is made on Earth, due to the pull of gravity, its chemicals and proteins don't mix properly or start settling down. In contrast, in space, medicines and proteins mix in pure form without any pull. This makes the process of making medicines extremely precise and clean. Engineers Leaving America-Europe and Coming to India After opening the space sector to private players, a new global trend is visible. Indian engineers working in America and Europe are now leaving their jobs and returning to India and joining the country's space startups. On this, PM Modi said that India should create an environment where the entire world's talent looks towards India to build a career in the space sector. articles.title: Bengaluru East Division police holds peace meeting ahead of Eid milad,St.Mary's Feast and ...
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain Ahead of the upcoming Eid Milad,St.Mary’s Feast and Ganesh Festival,Bengaluru East Division Police on Saturday held a coordination and peace meeting to ensure the festivals are celebrated peacefully and without inconvenience to the public. The meeting was held at Jalsa Banquet Hall, Pulakeshinagar,and was attended by the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner,Joint Commissioner of Police (East),DCP East,DCP Traffic East and senior officials from BESCOM,civic corporations,BMRCL,Forest Department,BWSSB,BMTC,Fire and Emergency Services and the Health Department. More than 250 people participated, including members of the Eid Milad Committee,St.Mary’s Basilica Feast Committee and various Ganeshotsava committees, besides religious leaders,public representatives and members of the public. Police and officials discussed arrangements to ensure that all three festivals are conducted with mutual respect,brotherhood and communal harmony. Officials issued instructions to take adequate precautionary measures, prevent untoward incidents, maintain law and order and minimise inconvenience to the public. Representatives of different religious communities assured the police of their cooperation in maintaining peace and social unity. Police also appealed to citizens not to believe or spread rumours and to immediately alert the authorities about any suspicious activity or incident. Officials from all concerned departments assured that necessary arrangements would be made for the smooth conduct of the festivals.
